enriched_description: Protective headgear for American football with hard plastic outer shell (glossy finish, team colors). Shell is rounded with extended ear coverage and facemask attachment points. Facemask is metal wire cage (chrome or colored) with horizontal and vertical bars forming grid pattern, attached via J-hooks. Interior padding is visible at edges: foam cushions and inflatable air bladders. Chin strap with 4-point attachment and buckle. Ventilation holes (circular) on top and sides. Decals: team logo on both sides, player number on front or back. Dimensions approximately 28x22x25 cm. Jaw pads extend downward at cheek area.

Industrial lift vehicle with front-mounted fork carriage. Body is compact cab (operator seat, steering wheel, overhead guard/cage) with counterweight at rear. Forks are two parallel steel tines (length 1-2 meters, width 10-15 cm) mounted on carriage that raises/lowers via hydraulic mast. Mast is vertical steel structure (2-6 meters tall) with chains and hydraulic cylinders. Color is yellow, orange, or red (safety colors). Power source: electric (battery compartment visible) or internal combustion (exhaust pipe). Rear wheels are smaller than front. Dimensions: 2-3 m long, 1-1.2 m wide.

Architectural water feature with sculptural basin and water jets. Basin is circular, rectangular, or tiered (multiple levels), constructed from stone (marble, granite, limestone), concrete, or metal. Water jets shoot upward from center or multiple points, creating spray patterns. Surface texture is smooth polished stone or rough-hewn natural stone. Decorative elements include sculpted figures (animals, mythological figures), ornamental spouts, and carved reliefs. Water surface reflects light, creating shimmering effect. Base may have stepped tiers with water cascading between levels. Surrounding area shows wet stone staining and splash patterns.

Writing instrument with internal ink reservoir and metal nib. Body is cylindrical barrel (length 13-15 cm, diameter 1-1.5 cm) constructed from resin, celluloid, metal, or ebonite. Nib is gold, steel, or iridium-tipped, visible when uncapped, with slit and breather hole. Cap fits over nib with clip for pocket attachment. Filling mechanism: piston, cartridge, converter, or eyedropper. Surface finish is glossy (resin), brushed (metal), or patterned (marbled, striped). Nib size markings (EF, F, M, B) engraved. Band details: metal rings at cap and barrel junction. Weight is balanced for writing comfort.

Bed with four vertical posts at each corner (height 180-250 cm above mattress). Posts are turned wood (decorative lathe-work: spiral, bulbous, or fluted profiles) or simple square/round columns. Top rails connect posts forming rectangular frame for canopy support. Bed frame is wooden (oak, mahogany, cherry) with headboard and footboard. Mattress sits within frame at standard height. Canopy fabric (if present) drapes from top rails, creating enclosed space. Wood finish is stained, polished, or painted. Posts may feature finials (decorative tops). Overall proportions are substantial, dominating bedroom space.

Railway vehicle for cargo transport. Boxcar variant: enclosed rectangular body (length 15-20 m) with sliding side doors, roof, and underframe. Surface is painted steel (various railroad colors) with visible rivet/weld seams. Couplers at both ends. Bogies (wheel assemblies) beneath at each end. Hopper car variant: open-top with sloped sides for bulk material discharge. Tank car: cylindrical tank on flatcar frame. Flatcar: open deck with stake pockets. Surface shows weathering, rust streaks, graffiti, and railroad markings (reporting marks, capacity data). Wheels are steel on steel rails.

Brass instrument with coiled conical tubing forming circular shape. Bell diameter 30-33 cm, facing backward and slightly downward. Total tubing length 3.7-5.5 meters (depending on F or Bb horn). Three or four rotary valves operated by lever keys on left side. Mouthpiece is funnel-shaped (deeper than trumpet), inserted into leadpipe. Body is lacquered brass (golden) or nickel-silver (silver). Hand rest on valve casing for left-hand support. Bell rim is rolled edge. Finger buttons are mother-of-pearl or plastic. Surface shows valve casing seams and tubing curves.

Shallow circular cooking pan (diameter 20-30 cm, depth 4-6 cm) with long handle. Material is cast iron (black, rough seasoned surface), stainless steel (polished silver), aluminum (brushed or anodized), or non-stick coated (black PTFE surface). Handle is metal (with heat-resistant grip) or Bakelite/plastic, attached by rivets or welded. Bottom is flat (induction-compatible) or slightly rounded. Sloped sides facilitate food flipping. Surface shows cooking residue patterns, oil sheen, or pristine non-stick coating. Handle length 15-20 cm with hanging hole at end.

Outer garment constructed from animal pelts (mink, fox, sable, chinchilla, or rabbit). Surface is dense, lustrous fur with natural color variation (brown, black, white, silver, or dyed). Fur length varies: short (mink, 1-2 cm) to long (fox, 5-10 cm). Coat length is hip-length to full-length (ankle). Construction shows horizontal or vertical pelting seams. Collar is wide, often matching fur. Lining is silk or satin (visible at edges and interior). Closure is hidden hooks, buttons, or belt. Sleeves are full-length with fur cuffs. Texture is soft, plush, with natural sheen.

Large waste collection vehicle with rear-loading, side-loading, or front-loading mechanism. Body is rectangular compactor unit (length 8-12 m) mounted on heavy-duty truck chassis. Color is green, white, or orange. Rear-loader variant shows hopper opening at back with hydraulic lift mechanism for bins. Side-loader has automated arm extending from side. Front-loader has fork arms at front for dumpster lifting. Compactor blade visible inside hopper. Cab is standard truck cab with large mirrors. Reflective safety markings and warning lights. Hydraulic cylinders and mechanisms visible on exterior.
